subject: Shadow run scope and timing — p95/p99 targets for hosted vs incumbent
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@helixhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Shadow run scope and timing — p95/p99 targets for hosted vs incumbent

Hi Maya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the shadow run: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Goal: validate end-to-end p95/p99 for your production traffic when routed to Redwood hosted API vs your incumbent.
- Target band you mentioned: p95 <= 200 ms, p99 <= 650 ms (end-to-end, client observed).
- Traffic profile: ~200 RPS sustained during peak, bursts to 350 RPS, average concurrent streaming sessions ~30-50.
- Key concerns: tail variance during multipart streaming responses and backend prefetch misses.

Proposed shadow run (redwood -> helix traffic mirror)
- Duration: 48 hours (48h window to capture diurnal and burst patterns).
- Mode: 10% mirrored traffic to Redwood hosted endpoints (no user impact).
- Traffic envelope: 200 RPS sustained; allow controlled bursts to 400 RPS for 10-15 min windows.
- Concurrency target: exercise up to 50 concurrent streaming sessions; include chunked SSE/HTTP2 streaming.
- Measurements: end-to-end latency (client start -> last byte), p95 and p99, request/response sizes, backend K/V cache hit rate, and server-side tail traces.

What we need from your side before kickoff
1) A 30-minute window to exchange trace ID mapping (to correlate Helix request IDs with HTTP client IDs).
2) A short trace sample (1-2 full request/response traces) — can be redacted — to validate our parsing.
3) Confirmation of preferred 48h window (we propose Tue-Wed next week).

Attachments: draft shadow-test-config.yaml (contains traffic scaling and sampling rates), and a latency envelope brief for our engineers.

Next steps / asks
- Maya: confirm you can provide the trace sample and whether the p95/p99 definition should include client network overhead.
- Ben/Camila: please review the draft config and confirm infra readiness (I copied you).

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0118

--

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@helixhealth.ai>

Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Shadow run scope and timing — p95/p99 targets for hosted vs incumbent

Thanks Soojin — helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Measurement definition: when we say end-to-end we include the client-side observed time (edge LB -> client last byte). Please call this out so we can compare apples-to-apples. Our current provider reports server-side only which hides client-edge variance.

2) Trace sample: attached a redacted trace-sample-20270917.json (small sample from yesterday). It includes our trace IDs and a snippet of headers. Hope that helps your parsing.

3) Scheduling: Tue-Wed next week is okay for the 48h window; can we start Tuesday 08:00 PDT? Procurement looped in for visibility — they may raise questions on data residency but for mirror traffic there shouldn't be persisted PHI.

One more ask: please include in the report a simple traffic breakdown by endpoint (tokenization, generation, streaming) — that helps our SREs understand where tails originate.

Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Product, Integrations | HelixHealth
maya.patel@helixhealth.ai
--

Forwarding Maya's reply and the trace sample. Engineering asks below — cc'ing Ben for capacity coordination.

Engineering ask (Dylan/Camila):
- Can you validate parsing for trace-sample-20270917.json and confirm we can correlate Helix trace IDs with our request IDs?
- Prep a shadow-run config: 10% mirror, header injection for trace ID mapping, sample rate 1:10 for full-body capture.
- Capture server-side traces with full call stacks and the following labels: redwood_request_id, helix_trace_id, upstream_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit (boolean), chunk_count (for streaming).
- Warm caches / preheat KV for the first 30 minutes of the window and include a warmup period in the analysis.
- Produce an initial runbook template for anomalies (if p99 spikes > +2x incumbent).

Ben: can you confirm we have capacity on the dedicated frontends for a 400 RPS burst simulation and the agent to inject trace headers?

I'll draft the kickoff note to Helix with proposed Tue 08:00 PDT start assuming all green.

Thanks,
Soojin

- Capacity: confirmed. We can sustain 10% mirrored load at 200 RPS with controlled 400 RPS bursts (we'll route to a separate pool to avoid interference).
- Tracing: Dylan will add the header mapping: X-Helix-Trace-Id -> redwood_request_id and we'll ingest the trace-sample to validate correlation.
